# Support ticket write-up template

Copy to `docs/case-studies/CS-NN-short-name.md`. Keep the customer-facing reply in plain language;
everything above it can be technical.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Ticket ID | CS-NN |
| Date opened / closed | YYYY-MM-DD / YYYY-MM-DD |
| Severity | P1 (results wrong or blocked for many) · P2 (one customer blocked) · P3 (workaround exists) · P4 (question) |
| Customer | (fictional) |
| Reported symptom | "The customer's own words, quoted." |

## 1. Summary

Two sentences a non-specialist could read: what happened and what we did about it.

## 2. Impact

- Which samples, runs or deliverables are affected?
- Has anything already been delivered that is wrong? If yes, who needs to be told, and by when?

## 3. Timeline

| When | What |
|---|---|
| | Reported |
| | First response |
| | Root cause found |
| | Resolved / customer confirmed |

## 4. Investigation

Commands run, in order, with the evidence each one produced (tables, read-level evidence,
igv-reports pages). Note dead ends too: they save the next person time.

## 5. Root cause

One paragraph. Distinguish *what* failed from *why* it was possible.

## 6. Resolution

What we did for this customer (re-run, corrected file, advice).

## 7. Prevention

The code, check or documentation change that stops this recurring, with a link to the commit.

## 8. Customer-facing reply

> The message as it would be sent. Lead with the answer, explain in plain language, say what we
> will do and by when, and say what we cannot promise.
